quote: Fairness and justice are also central. New genetic therapies are often extremely expensive. If genome editing becomes available mainly to those who can pay large sums, it could deepen existing health inequalities. There is also a global dimension: research priorities may focus on diseases that affect wealthy countries while neglecting conditions that affect poorer regions. Some argue that any future approval of genome editing should be accompanied by public funding, universal access and safeguards against discrimination by insurers or employers.
